result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.k_truss()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Extract the k-truss subgraph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16647-L16696){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.k_truss(k) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The k-truss is the maximal subgraph where every edge is part of at least `(k-2)` triangles. Iteratively removes edges with insufficient triangle support. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Minimum number of triangles + 2 for edges. Must be >= 3. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New graph containing only the k-truss edges and their endpoints. Isolated nodes are removed. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If k < 3. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#e9580cd7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph() for i in range(4): g.add_node(label=str(i)) # Create complete graph K4 for i in range(4): for j in range(i + 1, 4): g.add_edge(str(i), str(j)) # Get 4-truss (edges in >= 2 triangles) truss_4 = g.k_truss(4) # Returns the number of edges in the 4-truss truss_4.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 6 ``` ::: :::
